first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, directly mirroring a metric that two separate memories show we can move. Memory_31 (signup simplification) and memory_86 (shortening onboarding) both demonstrate durable lift in activation and time-to-value. The current situation shows onboarding completion erosion is a present, measurable problem. Simplifying onboarding is lower-risk than aggressive promotional pricing (which could devalue the brand against the competitor threat) and more defensible than referral incentives (which are best suited to healthy retention baselines). Activation messaging alone won't fix structural onboarding friction. Enterprise sales assist doesn't address the SMB segment hemorrhaging and activation decline. This experiment directly addresses a known failure mode with proven levers, stays focused on sustainable revenue quality, and preserves the ability to test pricing or messaging if onboarding gains don't cascade to activation recovery.

final.rationale: Archive validation confirms both memories. Memory_31 showed +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue on SMB signup simplification with only -1% retention risk. Memory_86 showed +13% completion, -2.1 day time-to-value, and +3% retention lift on shortened onboarding. The current 4% QoQ onboarding completion decline and 6% activation decline directly map to these proven intervention points. While competitor pricing pressure exists, onboarding simplification addresses structural product friction that weakens our defensibility regardless of pricing. The retention gains in memory_86 and minimal downside in memory_31 indicate this is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not a short-term tactical response. Running this experiment this week restores a degraded core metric while preserving optionality for pricing or messaging interventions based on results. The SMB-specific nature of memory_31 is noted but onboarding completion issues are segment-agnostic.
